sections.label: Categories of Presidential Elections amendments
sections.summary: The amendments fall into three categories: giving effect to the 2016 Constitutional amendments, improving Presidential election procedures, and aligning with Parliamentary Elections Act provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The first category of amendments gives effect to the amendments made by the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Act 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The second category of amendments improve election procedures during the conduct of Presidential elections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The third category of amendments aligns the Act with provisions of the Parliamentary Elections Act relating to election advertising, publication of election survey results and exit polls.

sections.label: Nomination day timing requirement
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 6(3) to require nomination day be at least 10 days after the Writ of Election date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Clause 4 amends section 6(3) to require that nomination day must be at least 10 days after the date of the Writ of Election.

sections.label: Community declaration deadline and Committee composition
sections.summary: The community declaration deadline is five days after the Writ of Election, and the 16-person Community Committee is appointed by the Prime Minister on PCMR nomination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The deadline for submission of the community declaration is five days after the date of the Writ of Election, similar to the deadline to apply for the Certificate of Eligibility to the PEC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Community Committee will consist of 16 persons: the Chairman; five members belonging to the Chinese community; five members belonging to the Malay community; and five members belonging to the Indian or Other Minority communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Chairman and members of the Community Committee will be appointed by the Prime Minister on the nomination of the Presidential Council for Minority Rights (PCMR).

sections.label: Limit on inviting another declaration
sections.summary: Where the Community Committee may invite the declarant to submit another community declaration, it may do so only once.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In both instances where the Community Committee may invite the declarant to submit another community declaration, it may only do so once.

sections.label: Voiding election for false statements
sections.summary: Clause 19 amends section 71 so an election can be declared void if the elected candidate made a materially false or misleading statement, or omitted a material fact, to PEC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Clause 19 amends section 71 to provide that an election can be declared void if the elected candidate made a materially false or misleading statement of fact, or omitted to state a material fact, to PEC.

sections.label: Extending overseas ballot box deadline
sections.summary: The amendments give the Returning Officer discretion to extend by seven days the time for overseas ballot boxes to reach Singapore if two conditions are fulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The amendments to that section confer a discretion on the Returning Officer to extend the time by another seven days for the overseas ballot boxes to reach Singapore if two conditions are fulfilled.

sections.label: Recount criteria for candidates
sections.summary: The law allows a candidate or counting agent to apply for a recount if the vote difference is 2% or less of total votes cast in Singapore, excluding rejected and tendered votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Currently, the law provides for a candidate or his counting agent to apply for a recount of votes if the criteria for recount is met, that is, if the difference between the number of votes given to the candidate with the most votes and the number of votes given to any other candidate at the election is 2% or less of the total number of votes cast in Singapore, excluding rejected votes and tendered votes, at the election.

sections.label: Lost or destroyed ballot boxes
sections.summary: If a sealed ballot box is lost or destroyed in transport, the Returning Officer must abandon counting all votes at that polling station and re-start the poll if material to the outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If any sealed ballot box containing votes cast at a polling station, whether in Singapore or overseas, is lost or destroyed while it is being transported from a polling station to a counting place, the Returning Officer must, first, abandon the counting of all the votes cast at the affected polling station, and this includes the votes cast at the affected polling station that were not in the lost or destroyed ballot box; and second, re-start the poll for the affected polling station if it will be material to the outcome of the election.

sections.label: Overseas elector registration deadline
sections.summary: The time for an elector to register as an overseas elector or change their overseas polling station is extended to two days after the Writ of Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The time within which an elector has to register as an overseas elector or apply to change the overseas polling station allotted to the elector is being extended to two days after the Writ of Election.

sections.label: Increased television airtime for candidates
sections.summary: The Government will increase the amount of television airtime for candidates and study different options to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To help candidates reach out to voters, the Government will increase the amount of television airtime for candidates and study different options to achieve this.

sections.label: No rally sites at Presidential elections
sections.summary: The Government will no longer designate any rally sites during Presidential elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government will no longer designate any rally sites during Presidential elections.

sections.label: Presidential election period announcement
sections.summary: The second announcement concerns the election period for the Presidential elections, and the current President's term expires on 31 August 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: My second announcement has to do with the election period for the Presidential elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The current President's term of office expires on 31 August 2017.

sections.label: Writ and polling day timing
sections.summary: The Government will issue the election writ in August 2017, so a contested election's polling day falls in September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government will issue the writ for the election later in August, before President Tony Tan's term expires on 31 August 2017 so that if the election is contested, polling day will take place in September instead of August.

sections.label: Acting President's one-month period
sections.summary: The acting President should exercise the President's functions for no more than one month, from 1 September 2017 until the elected President assumes office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The period during which the acting President shall exercise the functions of the office of President should not exceed one month, from 1 September 2017 to the date of assumption of office by the person declared elected as President.

sections.label: Reserved Malay presidential election
sections.summary: The upcoming Presidential election is reserved for Malay candidates, and a contest would mean Polling Day in September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The upcoming Presidential election has been reserved for Malay candidates and, should there be a contest, Polling Day will be held in September.

sections.label: Separating polling day timings
sections.summary: Presidential election Polling Day usually fell in late August, but this year's Polling Day will be in September to avoid a timing clash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In the past, the Polling Day of the Presidential elections typically fell in the last week of August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government feels that these two should happen separately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To prevent the clash of timings, this year's Polling Day will be in September.

sections.label: Refining the elected presidency system
sections.summary: The consultation process signals the Government's intent to refine the system, keep the presidency multiracial and unifying, and accept a reserved election recommendation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The time taken, along with the range of people that were consulted in the process, signals the Government's intent in refining the system and ensuring that the office of President is held by a person with the necessary qualities and experience to exercise the powers and duties of the highest office in the country; that the office of the President continues to reflect the multiracial nature of Singapore; and that this office continues to be a unifying symbol for all Singaporeans, regardless of race, language or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of the major changes was accepting the Commission's recommendation of the concept of a "reserved election" in the event a particular race had not had the chance to hold the office of President after five terms.

sections.label: Community Committee and sub-committees
sections.summary: The Bill creates a Community Committee of three sub-committees, each with five members, appointed by the Prime Minister on the Presidential Council for Minority Rights' nomination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In my speech, I will focus on these amendments, and given they are unique to Singapore, seek clarification on some of the areas that may be open to interpretation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill creates a new committee called the "Community Committee", a committee that is made up of three sub-committees, with five members from each of the Chinese, Malay and Indian and Other Minority committees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The language used in the proposed section 8E of the Bill is that this committee is to be appointed by the Prime Minister on the nomination of the Presidential Council for Minority Rights.

sections.label: Single community identification question
sections.summary: The Bill permits identifying with only one community, so a person identifying with more than one may have to decide and possibly change that decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill, as currently drafted, permits a person to identify with only one community but a person who identifies with more than one community may then have to make a decision and would this person then be able to change decision if, say, the reserved election were for different community in a subsequent term?

sections.label: Other Minority community definition
sections.summary: The speaker says Other Minority refers to established Singapore minority communities, not ethnicity, so a new citizen from a country with no community here would not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thus, everyone of mixed descent might feel they belong in this category based on ethnicity, whether or not they identify with a particular community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, I understand the original legislative intent when this category was created for the purposes of the GRC scheme was for this category to be based around minority communities that were established in Singapore and not based purely on ethnicity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thus, I believe the category "Other Minority" communities refers to a community that is established in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This would also mean, for example, we have, say, a foreign chief executive officer from a country with no community here who gets Singapore citizenship subsequently and decides he wants to apply, he would not qualify as a member of the "Other Minority" communities' category for purposes of a reserved election, but would still be able to apply in an open election under section 8F(2)(d).

sections.label: Other Minority factors clarification
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify what factors determine an Other Minority community and whether it is not a catch-all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What would be the factors to be taken into account in determining whether a particular community is one of the "Other Minority" communities for purposes of section 8F(2)(c) of the amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, be grateful for the Minister's clarification that the definition of "Other Minority" communities, as a provision, is not intended to be a "catch-all" for people who do not fit into the other categories by ethnicity, but is intended to be only for those who are part of the established minority communities in Singapore.

sections.label: Reserved election for Malays
sections.summary: The Schedule counts President Wee Kim Wee first, and with later non-Malay terms forming five, the Government concludes this year's election is reserved for Malays.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Schedule sets out a table showing President Wee Kim Wee as the first President to be counted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Together with the subsequent presidential terms of President Ong Teng Cheong, two terms of President SR Nathan and one term of President Tony Tan, these formed five terms where a non-Malay President was in office.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thus, the Government reaches the conclusion that this year's Presidential election will be reserved for Malays.

sections.label: Shareholders equity and profit definitions
sections.summary: Section 5C defines shareholders' equity, profit after tax and insolvency events, needed for the new requirement of running profitable companies with at least $500 million equity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 5C touches on the definitions of shareholders' equity, profit after tax and insolvency events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These definitions are needed due to the new requirement for candidates to have run companies of shareholders' equity of at least $500 million which have been profitable.

sections.label: Community declaration eligibility conditions
sections.summary: New eligibility conditions require all candidates, including ethnic Chinese, to submit a community declaration to a 16-member Community Committee before ethnicity is confirmed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: New conditions have been included in the eligibility criteria, including the ethnic Chinese, all candidates need to submit a community declaration to a 16-member Community Committee, and they can only be considered eligible for an election after their ethnicity has been confirmed.

sections.label: Reserved election for Malay candidates
sections.summary: Since none of the five Presidents from Mr Wee Kim Wee onwards was Malay, the next Presidential election will be reserved for Malay candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From our first elected President Mr Wee Kim Wee onwards, none of our five Presidents was a Malay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the next Presidential election will be reserved for Malay candidates.

sections.label: Extending nomination and election period
sections.summary: Because the next Presidential election is unique and the President's ability to unite Singaporeans is uncertain, the nomination and election period should be extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whether the President can command the respect and admiration of all Singaporeans and can unite Singaporeans to forge a better tomorrow, could be a question mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I suggest that due to the unique nature of the next Presidential election, the nomination and election period should be extended, allowing more people to understand the background of the candidates.

sections.label: Community Committee for reserved elections
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a Community Committee to determine, in a reserved election, whether a person belongs to the community the election is reserved for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the most significant aspects of this Bill is the establishment of a Community Committee which ensures that, in a reserved election, only persons who see themselves as belonging to a particular community for which the election is reserved, qualify to stand for the Presidential election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the PEC and, by extension, the Community Committee's decisions are not justiciable in a Court of law, Parliament is effectively the last place for Singaporeans to gain an insight into how the Community Committee and sub-committees will operate in practice, and how decisions are made by these committees in reserved elections will be the focus of my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 8(g) is scant on details as to how the relevant Community Committee/sub-committees will assess a potential candidate as to whether he or she is a member of a particular minority community.

sections.label: Minority candidates and public sector track
sections.summary: Because minority candidates are likely few, many will likely enter Presidential elections through the public sector track rather than the private sector track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifthly, Mdm Speaker, I take the position that because minority candidates are likely to be few to begin with, many candidates are likely to enter Presidential elections through the public sector track or public sector deliberative track rather than the more stringent private sector track with its $500 million threshold.

sections.label: Criteria for public sector deliberative track
sections.summary: The Government should share the criteria the PEC uses to determine if a public sector deliberative track minority candidate qualifies for candidature as President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What this point does reiterate however, is the importance of the Government sharing what criteria would be used by PEC to determine if a public sector deliberative track minority candidate qualifies for candidature as President in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in the case of Mdm Speaker, should the hon Speaker decide to stand as a candidate, what happens to the very existence of Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC which, by law, requires a Malay MP as one of its political representatives in Parliament?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should it be passed, does this Bill herald a new precedent in marked contrast to the scenario in Jurong GRC some years ago when the late PAP MP Mr Ong Chit Chung passed on?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Bill and the prospect of reserved Presidential elections change the Government's thinking on the question: will a by-election be called in a GRC when the minority member of a GRC steps down to contest in a Presidential election?

sections.label: Abandoning ballots from lost boxes
sections.summary: Clause 15 proposes abandoning counting of ballots cast at a polling station if a ballot box is lost or destroyed in transit, and restarting polling if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 15 of the Bill proposes to abandon the counting of ballots cast at a polling station if one of the ballot boxes is lost or destroyed in transit from the polling station to a counting centre, and to restart the polling, if necessary.

sections.label: Restarting voting at affected polling station
sections.summary: Voting at an affected polling station restarts if the two leading candidates' vote difference is less than the sum of allotted electors and overseas electors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The voting for the affected polling station would be restarted if the difference in the vote count of the two leading Presidential candidates, without counting the votes cast at the affected polling station, is less than the sum of: (a) the total number of electors allotted to the affected polling station and entitled to vote in the election; and (b) the total number of overseas electors entitled to vote in the election.

sections.label: 2011 Presidential Election vote margin
sections.summary: In the 2011 Presidential Elections, the difference between ballots for Tony Tan and Tan Cheng Bock was about 7,000 votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the last Presidential Elections of 2011, the difference between the ballots cast for President Tony Tan and Dr Tan Cheng Bock was just some 7,000 votes.

sections.label: Minister's discretion on re-vote scope
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister may decide if all allotted electors vote again or only those of the lost or destroyed ballot box.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does this mean the Minister would have the discretion to decide whether all electors allotted to the affected polling station would vote again upon the restart of polls, or limit the re-vote to only the electors allotted to the lost or destroyed ballot box?

sections.label: Constitutional amendments on Elected Presidency passed
sections.summary: After three days of parliamentary debates, amendments to the Constitution changing the Elected Presidency were passed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: After three days of debates in Parliament, amendments to the Constitution that made changes to the Elected Presidency were passed.

sections.label: Further community declaration invitation request
sections.summary: Clause 8H(9) suggests an applicant may not make another community declaration after rejection except on the Community Committee's invitation, prompting a question on requesting a further invitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, clause 8H(9) appears to suggest that the applicant may not make another community declaration upon rejection except on the invitation of the Community Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the applicant request for a further invitation?

sections.label: Support for Commission's campaign proposals
sections.summary: The speaker sees merit in the Commission's proposals against divisive campaigning and misinformation, and welcomes amendments in clauses 6 and 17.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I see merit in the proposals made by the Commission to avoid divisive campaigning and giving misinformation about the President's role to the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome and am happy to note the amendments that clause 6, with regard to the statutory declarations required of the candidate, and clause 17 on election advertising.

sections.label: Banning election surveys and exit polls
sections.summary: The speaker cites Trump's unexpected win over Clinton to support banning election surveys and exit polls from Writ of Election to polling close.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: History repeated itself when the majority of the opinion polls in the United States had predicted a win for Mrs Hillary Clinton but Mr Trump won surprisingly and convincingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These are the reasons why I support the insertion of sections 60B and 60C under clause 18 to ban election surveys and exit polls for the period between the issuance of Writ of Election and the close of all the polling stations on the polling day of the election.

sections.label: Presidential candidate declaration of role
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister which aspects of the President's role would be stated in the prescribed form candidates must understand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to move on to the proposed amendments in section 9 of the Bill under clause 6 which proposes that every hopeful Presidential candidate has to declare in his nomination papers that "he understands the President's role under the Constitution, including any particular aspect of the President's role stated in the prescribed form." I would like to clarify with the Minister: which aspects of the President's role would be stated in the prescribed form, which the candidate is expected to understand?

sections.label: Doubling TV broadcast frequency
sections.summary: The speaker says TV broadcast frequency should at least be doubled compared to the last Presidential Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Since TV broadcast will be the main channel by which the candidates can reach the voters, the TV broadcast frequency should at least be doubled, compared to the last Presidential Election.

sections.label: Postponing Presidential election polling day
sections.summary: The speaker supports postponing polling day, noting the Council of Presidential Advisers Chairman becomes Acting President when Dr Tony Tan steps down on 31 August 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For this reason, I support the proposal to postpone the polling day of the Presidential election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: When Dr Tony Tan steps down as the President on 31 August 2017, the Chairman of the Council of Presidential Advisers will assume the role of the Acting President, until the new President is elected in mid or end September.

sections.label: Assurance on Acting President powers
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill but seeks assurance that the Government will not ask the Acting President to exercise custodial powers during the September transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To be sensible, there is no need to rush to access Past Reserves or to appoint key Government officials so hastily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I hope that the Minister can assure us that the Government will not ask the Acting President to exercise his custodial powers during the September transition period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In English): In summary, I support the Bill and I applaud the early announcement on the changes to the election rules of the Presidential Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I hope that the Minister can clarify the purpose of asking the Presidential candidate to declare their understanding of the President's role as stated in the Constitution and the implications of the declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like the Minister to assure Singaporeans that the Government would not exploit the potential weakness of the system during the September period before the next Elected President takes office.

sections.label: Community Committee decision finality and immunity
sections.summary: The speaker notes the Community Committee's decision is final and not appealable, and it has comprehensive immunity except for malice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As per section 8J(2), the Community Committee's decision is final and not subject to any appeal or review by the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, the Community Committee is granted very comprehensive immunity as well, subject to the exception of malice, which is a high threshold to satisfy in a procedural or administrative context.

sections.label: Community Committee appointment defect
sections.summary: A defect in appointing a Community Committee member would not invalidate any of its proceedings, and the Bill operationalises constitutional changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I note that a defect in the appointment of any member of the Community Committee would not invalidate "any proceedings of the Community Committee".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Like how the Community Committee determines if a person is of a particular community, the PEC functions as another gatekeeper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As I emphasised at the start of my speech, this Bill makes amendments to the Presidential Elections Act that operationalise the changes that were made to the Constitution in November last year.

sections.label: Diverse Community Committee
sections.summary: The Government agrees the Community Committee must be diverse and each sub-committee representative of the community it represents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, the Government agrees that the Community Committee has to be diverse and each sub-committee has to be representative of the community it represents.

sections.label: Community declaration application process
sections.summary: Regulations will set out the certificate application process and information required, but the Community Committee will not release its grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The regulations will also set out the process for applying for the certificates and the information to be furnished by the prospective candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: However, we will not be making the Community Committee release grounds as to why it decides to accept or not accept the community declaration of a prospective candidate.

sections.label: PEC reasons for rejection
sections.summary: The Government broadly agreed the PEC should set out its grounds when rejecting an application but not publicise them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Commission suggested that "a more measured solution would be to require the PEC to furnish to the unsuccessful applicant its reasons for denying the Certificate of Eligibility, and to leave the applicant to decide for himself or herself whether he or she wishes to make those reasons public." The Government broadly agreed with this suggestion in the White Paper; the PEC should set out its grounds when it rejects a prospective candidate's application, but not publicise it.

sections.label: Other minority communities meaning
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean said other minority communities refer to groups with history, permanence and established presence, such as Eurasians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean provided an answer to this in the debates on the Constitutional Amendments last November.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: He made clear then that the "other minority communities" refer to groups that have some degree of history, permanence and established presence in Singapore, such as the Eurasian community.

sections.label: Administrative guidelines for applicants
sections.summary: Administrative guidelines will be provided to applicants to give clarity and certainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To give clarity and certainty, we will provide administrative guidelines to the applicants.

sections.label: No First Lady position
sections.summary: The passage states that constitutionally there is no such thing as a First Lady position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, constitutionally, there is no such thing as a First Lady position.

sections.label: Minority Members in House
sections.summary: The passage states that about one-third of the House is made up of minority Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we have about one-third of our House with minority Members.

sections.label: Minority MPs numbers
sections.summary: The passage states there are 25 minority Members of Parliament out of 89 elected, and 24 out of 89 is 27% of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, we have 25 minority Members of Parliament out of 89 elected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Even if we have one less, there are 24 out of 89, which is 27% of Parliament.

sections.label: Polling station as lowest unit
sections.summary: The passage states the polling station is the lowest unit because voters can drop ballots in any box there, so polls restart for an affected polling station if a box is destroyed and numbers are material.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To Mr Chen Show Mao, the polling station is the lowest unit because voters can drop their ballot papers in any of the ballot boxes in the polling station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why even if one box is destroyed and the number of the voters in the polling station is material to the outcome of the election results, we will restart the polls for the affected polling station.

sections.label: Commission proposals on President candidates
sections.summary: The passage states the Commission proposed laws requiring candidates to declare understanding of the President's constitutional role, making incompatible promises an offence, and imposing sanctions, but the Government decided to take up only the statutory declaration proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Commission proposed that laws be enacted, which: (a) require candidates to explicitly declare that they understand the constitutional role of the President before they may be issued a Certificate of Eligibility in the form of a statutory declaration contained within the application form for the Certificate of Eligibility (CoE); (b) make it an offence for candidates to make promises or to take positions that are incompatible with the office of President; and (c) impose a regime of sanctions where a breach of election rules, including a breach of the prohibition in (b), could give rise to a range of possible consequences, including criminal sanctions, applications to an Election Judge for declaratory reliefs, and, in appropriate extreme cases, the revocation of a candidate's Certificate of Eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Although the Commission suggested criminal sanctions, the Government has decided to take up the first proposal of requiring the statutory declaration.

sections.label: Additional TV airtime for candidates
sections.summary: The passage states the Government will increase national TV airtime for candidates, discuss additional airtime with Mediacorp, and consider a suggestion on at least two televised debates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government will increase the overall national TV airtime that candidates will have to allow the candidates a wide platform to share their views with the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government will discuss the provision of additional airtime for the candidates with Mediacorp.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will consider Mr Ang Wei Neng's suggestion on at least two televised debates when we discuss the format of the additional TV time with Mediacorp.

sections.label: Acting President when office vacant
sections.summary: Article 22N provides that the Chairman of the Council of Presidential Advisers, or the Speaker if unavailable, exercises the President's functions while the office is vacant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: According to Article 22N of the Constitution, if the office of the President becomes vacant, the Chairman of the Council of Presidential Advisers or, if he is unavailable, the Speaker, shall exercise the functions of the office of the President during the period between the date the office of President becomes vacant and the assumption of the office by the person declared elected as President.

sections.label: Government convention on Elected President
sections.summary: The Government will observe a convention respecting the Elected President's role as second key to the Reserves and key appointments, except when absolutely necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government will be observing a convention in relation to the Elected President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Unless absolutely necessary, for example, in a crisis situation that requires the use of the Reserves, the Government will respect that the rationale of the Elected Presidency is for an Elected President to be the second key to the Reserves and to key appointments.

sections.label: Changes to Elected Presidency
sections.summary: The Government believes the changes ensure the office is held by someone meeting stringent criteria, preserving meritocracy, and by persons of different communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government believes that the changes to the Elected Presidency will continue to ensure that the office will be held by someone who fulfils the stringent qualification criteria, ensuring meritocracy is not compromised, and will also be held by persons of different communities, reflecting the multiracial nature of Singapore.

sections.label: Eligibility criteria for private sector candidates
sections.summary: A Member says the Minister did not directly address the point that the November Constitution (Amendment) Bill required Parliament to define profit after tax, shareholders' equity and insolvency events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The first clarification concerns the eligibility criteria for private sector candidates running for President.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I do not think the Minister has addressed my point directly and that is that the Constitution (Amendment) Bill that was passed in November specifically asked Parliament to make these definitions: to define the definition of profit after tax, and also shareholders' equity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Bill in last November also required Parliament to prescribe what amounts to an insolvency event.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But what we find in the Bill today is that Parliament is passing this job on to the Minister to do and the purported guidelines in section 5C(2) and (3) are too general.

sections.label: Wee Kim Wee as first Elected President
sections.summary: The Member says people find it hard to understand why Wee Kim Wee counts as the first Elected President.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: My point was simply that people find it hard to understand why Wee Kim Wee counts as the first Elected President.

sections.label: Counting from President Wee Kim Wee
sections.summary: The Member notes clients can waive confidentiality and asks for more illumination on why counting starts from President Wee Kim Wee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But the fact also remains that clients can choose to waive the confidentiality if they find that there is a purpose in publishing it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I am just asking for more illumination on why we are counting from President Wee Kim Wee.

sections.label: Reserved election counting start explained
sections.summary: Counting starts from President Wee Kim Wee's second term because he was the first President to exercise powers under the new Elected Presidency Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second point about the reserved election, I am glad that Ms Lim has confirmed that she is not casting any aspirations on Prime Minister Lee's integrity and if that is the case then the Prime Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister, Mr Teo Chee Hean, have explained in November why the counting starts from the second term of President Wee Kim Wee's term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is because President Wee Kim Wee was the first President to exercise the powers under the new Elected Presidency Act.

sections.label: Government acting on Constitutional Commission reason
sections.summary: The Government decided to act in this term because the Constitutional Commission said it is the Government's onus to act decisively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As what the Constitutional Commission says, if there is a reason for us to act, then it is the onus of this Government to act in the best interest of this country decisively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why we have decided to do it in this term of Government.

sections.label: President's stabiliser and custodial role
sections.summary: The President's role is to serve as a stabiliser and to serve custodial functions over the country's Reserves and key appointments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Because his role is to serve as a stabiliser, his role is to serve the custodial functions for this country in terms of its Reserves and key appointments.

sections.label: Pledge of allegiance by all citizens
sections.summary: Every Singaporean, whether new or old citizen, makes the same pledge of allegiance to this country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Every Singaporean, regardless of whether new citizens or old citizens, make the same pledge of allegiance to this country.

sections.label: Representing Singaporeans and Community Committee precedent
sections.summary: Whether candidates best represent and unite Singaporeans is left to the electorate's judgement, and the Community Committee follows established precedent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As to whether they can best represent and unite Singaporeans, I think it is best left to the judgement of the Singaporean electorate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The question about how the Community Committee works, I think we have established precedent because this is how we have assessed the eligibility of the Malay candidates and the Indian and the Other Minority candidates for the Parliamentary elections in the past.

sections.label: Workers' Party Appointed President proposal
sections.summary: The Workers' Party proposed an Appointed President and an Elected Senate to exercise custodial powers over Civil Service appointments and the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The Workers' Party's proposal was for an Appointed President and an Elected Senate to exercise the custodial powers over Civil Service appointments and the Reserves that the Elected President currently holds.

sections.label: Appointed President versus Elected Presidency
sections.summary: The speaker says he did not support an Elected Presidency and argued for an Appointed President to avoid politicisation risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But I think even as your own extract makes clear, referring back to the debate that Deputy Prime Minister Teo cited, I did not support the idea of an Elected Presidency and making procedural changes to reduce the politicisation risk in the election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I and my colleagues argued for the idea of an Appointed President because we argued and we still maintain that if you have an election, inevitably, that politicisation risk will emerge.

sections.label: Reverting to Appointed President
sections.summary: The speaker states his position then and now is to revert to an Appointed President because procedural changes do not eliminate political risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The position that I articulated then, and I hold the same position now is that we should revert to an Appointed President because whatever procedural changes you make, you do not eliminate the political risk.

sections.label: Reply on politicisation risk strategy
sections.summary: The speaker quotes his reply agreeing with Mr Leon Perera on looking at rules for conducting Presidential Elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I have not heard any strategy from any Member of the PAP on how this can be managed".

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And it is quite clear, Mdm Speaker, that he is referring to electing the President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, what would be the Government's strategy to mitigate that?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: That is my second question." And, Madam, in my reply to him, I said, "Turning to the risk of politicisation and the possible tightening of rules for the Presidential Elections, the risk of politicisation is that I have already addressed it explicitly just now in my answer but I think what Mr Leon Perera suggests and what the Commission suggests also is to look at the rules and the way that the Presidential Elections are conducted, I think there is merit and I agree with Mr Leon Perera there." As I said, Madam, Mr Perera is not shy to stand up to disagree if he has been understood wrongly and he did not stand up to disagree with me at that point in time.

sections.label: Workers' Party dissent recorded
sections.summary: The Workers' Party Members ask that their dissent be specifically recorded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Workers' Party Members would like our dissent specifically recorded.

sections.label: Dissent recorded and abstention
sections.summary: The Workers' Party Members repeat their request to record dissent and ask to voice an abstention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Yes, Mdm Speaker, the Workers' Party Members would like our dissent specifically recorded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Can I voice my abstention to this vote?

sections.label: Not convinced by arguments
sections.summary: The speaker says he is still not convinced by the arguments for something.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Yes, because I am still not convinced by the arguments for —
